title: Transformer Models for Text Summarization: A Comparative Study of BART, BERT, and RoBERTa
abstract: arXiv:2608.19200v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Text summarization refers to the task of condensing a document into a shorter version while preserving its key information. Automatic text summarization (ATS), driven by advancements in natural language processing (NLP), has developed rapidly in recent years. ATS methods are commonly categorized by input type (such as single-document or multi-document summarization) and by output type (extractive, abstractive, and hybrid). This article presents a focused review of modern summarization techniques with an emphasis on transformer based models and large language models (LLMs), specifically BERT, RoBERTa and BART. It examines their architectures, pretraining strategies, and their suitability for extractive and abstractive summarization tasks.

translated_title: 用于文本摘要的Transformer模型：BART、BERT和RoBERTa的比较研究
translated_abstract: 文本摘要是指将文档压缩为较短版本同时保留其关键信息的任务。近年来，在自然语言处理（NLP）进步的推动下，自动文本摘要（ATS）发展迅速。ATS方法通常根据输入类型（如单文档或多文档摘要）和输出类型（抽取式、生成式和混合式）进行分类。本文对现代摘要技术进行了重点综述，特别关注基于Transformer的模型和大语言模型（LLMs），具体包括BERT、RoBERTa和BART。文章考察了它们的架构、预训练策略，以及它们在抽取式和生成式摘要任务中的适用性。
tldr: 本文比较了BERT、RoBERTa和BART等Transformer模型在文本摘要任务中的架构、预训练策略及适用性，强调了它们对抽取式和生成式摘要的各自优势。
en_tdlr: This article compares Transformer models like BERT, RoBERTa, and BART for text summarization, focusing on their architectures, pretraining strategies, and suitability for extractive and abstractive tasks.
